title: [Task Sprint] QA Testing Report — GoThru Photo Studio Tauri

issues.main_description_html:
COMPARE WITH FINDER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-06.at.15.03.58.mov

Problem

PR #143 fixes the four problems raised in the team feedback — large folders being slow, files that cannot be deleted or renamed, having to click Reload after every external change, and NAS drives mounted over the network. All four share one root: network volumes were treated exactly like local disks.

It passes the static gates only — cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo fmt, pnpm typecheck, and cargo test --lib commands::files (8 passed, including a new UNC normalisation test). The thing it actually fixes has not been exercised. A real SMB share, a Windows machine and a second machine writing into the same folder are not reachable from a test runner, and the Win32 call sites (GetDriveTypeW, GetLogicalDrives) are cross-compile verified only — they have never been executed.

What needs hands on it:

  • UNC paths — normalize_target_ext used to squeeze the leading // of \\NAS\share\photos into one slash and then strip it, leaving the relative NAS/share/photos. Any share not mapped to a drive letter simply would not open. Only a real share proves the round-trip: opening it, navigating into subfolders, and going back up.
  • Polling watcher — network folders now watch through notify::PollWatcher at a 5 s interval, because macOS FSEvents reports nothing at all for an SMB mount. Whether 5 s feels right, and whether polling a large folder costs anything noticeable, is a judgement only real use makes.
  • File locking — thumbnail prewarming is capped at 200 images and skipped entirely on network volumes, and watcher::release_dir now drops the watcher before a destructive op touches the watched folder. Both are Windows handle-semantics fixes (std::fs opens without FILE_SHARE_DELETE); on macOS they cannot fail the way they did for the user.
  • Large folders — the directory scan moved to the blocking pool and now reuses the metadata read_dir already returned instead of stat'ing every entry twice. Over SMB that removes one round-trip per file; the size of the win only shows on a real share.

What to do

Run on Windows, against an actual NAS share, on a real build (pnpm tauri dev or a release build — note which). Prepare a folder of a few thousand images on the share, a second machine (or a second Explorer window) able to write into it, and files you do not mind sending to the recycle bin. Work on copies.

  • N1 — UNC path opens. Type \\NAS\share into the path bar. The folder lists. Navigate into a subfolder and back out. (Before this PR: nothing opened at all.)
  • N2 — mapped drive opens. Same share mapped to a drive letter (e.g. Z:). Still lists, still navigates.
  • N3 — external add. With the share open in the app, create a file in that folder from the other machine. It appears in the grid within ~5 s, without touching Reload.
  • N4 — external delete. Delete a file from the other machine. It disappears from the grid within ~5 s, without Reload.
  • N5 — local folder unaffected. Repeat N3/N4 on a local folder. Changes still appear immediately (native watcher, not the poller) — this is the regression check on the watcher split.
  • N6 — delete during load. Open a large folder and delete a file from the grid while it is still filling in. The delete succeeds; no "file in use".
  • N7 — rename the open folder. Rename the folder currently open in the app, from the app and again from Explorer. Both succeed. (This is the watcher directory-handle fix.)
  • N8 — delete the open folder. Same, with delete to recycle bin.
  • N9 — large folder responsiveness. Open a folder with a few thousand images on the share. The window stays responsive while it lists; note roughly how long the listing takes so we have a number to compare against.
  • N10 — "My Computer" with a dead mapped drive. Disconnect the NAS but leave the drive letter mapped, then open "My Computer". It lists at once instead of hanging for tens of seconds.

Expected

Every row passes, or fails into its own issue.

N6, N7 and N8 are the blocker rows — they are the "locking files" complaint the user actually reported. If any of them still fails, that is the finding worth chasing before the rest.

Note

Also worth watching while testing: thumbnails on a network folder are now fetched only for the cards the grid displays, so scrolling fast through a NAS folder should show placeholders filling in behind you. That is intended. Thumbnails failing to appear at all, or a folder that never finishes listing, is not.

A mac pass on an SMB mount is useful as a second data point (N1 as /Volumes/..., N3–N5, N9), but the locking rows are Windows-only by nature.

This is the gate before PR #143 merges.

issues.display_title: Issue #168: get-raw-exif and get-file-on-folder still run on the main thread, freezing the window on network shares
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.25.12.mov

Two commands still do their filesystem work on the main thread, so the window is frozen for the whole duration. On a local disk this is invisible; on a network share every operation is a round-trip and the freeze becomes seconds.

Why a sync command freezes the window

A #[tauri::command] pub fn (no async) runs on the main thread, for as long as it takes. Traced through the dependency versions this repo pins:

  • tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.3/src/lib.rs:5197 — webview custom protocols are registered with wry's with_asynchronous_custom_protocol. "Asynchronous" only defers the response; the handler closure still fires on the UI thread.
  • tauri-2.11.3/src/manager/webview.rs:282 — the ipc scheme goes through that same registration.
  • tauri-2.11.3/src/ipc/protocol.rs:38 — get calls webview.on_message(...) inline, which calls manager.run_invoke_handler(invoke) inline. No spawn anywhere on the path.
  • tauri-macros-2.6.3/src/command/wrapper.rs:429 — body_blocking expands to let result = $path(args);, called inline.

This is the same class of bug as the asset:// protocol handler fixed in 6aadddb, just entering through the IPC path instead.

Remaining commands

1. get-raw-exif — src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs:605

Opens the same file five times, all on the main thread:

  • path.exists() — 1 round-trip
  • metadata_for(path_str) — fs::metadata, imagesize::size, read_exif, jpeg_sof (reads 256 KB) = 4 more

Single file, so roughly 15 ms on a wired NAS and up to ~150 ms over WiFi. Noticeable stutter each time the raw-EXIF popup opens, not fatal.

Callers: src/renderer/features/preview/RawExifPopup.tsx:61, src/renderer/components/features/Edit/Stitching/hooks/useStitching.ts:275.

2. get-file-on-folder — src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs:203

read_dir plus a p.is_file() per entry, serial, on the main thread. Structurally identical to the load-files problem fixed in 6aadddb — this command just never got the same treatment.

Worse than get-raw-exif because it scales with folder size, and every caller runs it over a folder the user picked for a batch job:

  • src/renderer/components/features/Edit/CubeToEquirectangular/ProgressList.tsx:174
  • src/renderer/components/features/Edit/MinifyJpg/hooks/useMinifyJpgAddToQueue.ts:77
  • src/renderer/components/features/Edit/Enfuse/hooks/useEnfuseQueue.ts:225

Fix

Same mechanical shape already applied to the batch commands on fix/nas:

  • pub fn → pub async fn
  • body into tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking
  • par_iter where there is a per-entry loop (get-file-on-folder)

For get-raw-exif there is a second, optional win: jpeg_sof already reads 256 KB, which is enough to satisfy imagesize and the EXIF parser too. Folding the four opens into one would cut it to a single round-trip — worth measuring after the spawn_blocking change, not before.

Guard against regressions

New commands that touch the filesystem should default to pub async fn + spawn_blocking. A sync command is only safe when it does no I/O at all (generate_uuid, is_windows) or exactly one stat on a path that is always local.

Deliberately out of scope — single-file stat, not loops, so they cannot freeze for more than one round-trip:

  • room_staging_check_overwrite (src-tauri/src/commands/room_staging.rs:649)
  • virtual_staging_2d_check_overwrite (src-tauri/src/commands/virtual_staging_2d.rs:162)
  • get_file_stats, create_folder, rename_image, rename_file_or_folder, check_directory_exists
  • resolve_path_to_absolute (src-tauri/src/commands/system.rs:66) — up to 3 stats plus a canonicalize, which resolves per path component over SMB. Upper bound worth remembering if path resolution ever shows up in a profile.

QA Summary — Bug Found

QA date: 2026-09-02
Target: GoThru Photo Studio desktop app (Tauri v2 + Rust) / Issue #168 — get-raw-exif and get-file-on-folder main thread blocking
Verdict: Failed — coding bug confirmed.

Executive Summary

Code review and runtime validation on Windows 11 with SMB network mount (Z:\) confirm that both get_raw_exif and get_file_on_folder still execute filesystem I/O synchronously on the UI / main thread. On network shares with high round-trip latency, this causes visible UI frame drops and temporary window freezing when opening the Raw EXIF modal in Preview or selecting input folders for batch processing.

TC-02 White-box Review signature & directory iteration of get_file_on_folder in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs Directory scan runs off-thread via spawn_blocking with parallel entry evaluation (par_iter) std::fs::read_dir loop runs serially without thread pool offload Fail (Bug)
TC-03 Black-box Open Raw EXIF modal on network photo (Z:\Work\qa-nas-test\image_1.jpg) in Preview Modal opens smoothly without UI thread stutter or frame drops Successfully extracts 8 EXIF tags, but 5 sequential network roundtrips occur on the UI dispatch thread Fail (Bug)
TC-04 Black-box Select large network folder (50 photos) in Z:\Work\qa-nas-test\large_folder for batch processing Directory reading completes asynchronously without UI stall All 50 files returned, but serial iteration holds the caller thread Fail (Bug)

Scales with folder size and stalls the executor thread on large NAS folders. Wrap directory reading inside tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking and utilize par_iter() for non-blocking parallel classification.

issues.display_title: Issue #160: Copy and move into a mounted USB or network volume silently do nothing
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.45.16.mov

What happens

In the File Manager, copying or moving files into a panel pointed at a mounted volume (USB stick, or an SMB/network share) does nothing at all. No file appears at the destination, and no error or toast is shown — the operation looks like it was ignored.

Root cause: resolve_dest in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs anchored the renderer's display-relative currentDirectory at $HOME unconditionally. Mounted volumes are anchored at the volumes root instead (/Volumes on macOS, /media on Linux), so a destination of sambashare resolved to $HOME/sambashare, which does not exist, and the command returned error: "Destination folder does not exist.".

The listing side already handles both anchors — normalize_target_ext in src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs falls back to the volumes root when the home anchor does not exist. Copy and move never got that treatment, so browsing a volume worked while writing to it did not.

Second defect, which is why it failed silently: copySources and moveSources in src/renderer/features/fileManager/hooks/useFileOperations.ts only report a failure from .catch(). The command resolves with error set rather than rejecting, so the error branch never ran.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a network share (SMB) or plug in a USB drive.
  2. Open File Manager and point the right panel at the volume (My Computer → the volume, e.g. sambashare).
  3. Select any file in the left panel (e.g. under Documents) and press Copy.
  4. Nothing arrives in the right panel. No toast, no error, no entry.

Copying into an ordinary folder under the home directory works, which is what makes this look like a NAS/permissions problem rather than a path bug. Verified it is not permissions: cp, mkdir, xattr and cp -p all succeed against the same mount from a terminal.

Goal

  1. Copy and move into a mounted USB or network volume write the files to the volume.
  2. Copy and move into ordinary home-relative folders behave exactly as before.
  3. Same-name conflicts still route through the existing overwrite modal.
  4. A copy or move that fails surfaces a toast instead of failing silently.

QA Summary — Passed

QA date: 2026-09-02
Target: GoThru Photo Studio desktop app (Tauri v2 + Rust) / Issue #160 — Copy and move into a mounted USB or network volume
Verdict: Passed.

Executive Summary

End-to-end real-device testing on Windows 11 with live mapped SMB shares (Z:\), UNC volumes, and local folders confirms full resolution of Issue #160:

  1. Volume Path Resolution: resolve_dest in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs now delegates to files::normalize_target, properly handling mounted volume roots and network shares instead of unconditionally prepending $HOME.
  2. Copy & Move Operations: Files copy and move into mapped network shares (Z:\Work\qa-nas-test) and back to local directories cleanly with 100% data integrity.
  3. Error Reporting & Toast Feedback: useFileOperations.ts checks res.error and triggers user-facing toast notifications when destination paths do not exist instead of failing silently.

All 4 test scenarios (TC-01 through TC-04) executed and passed on the real application with 100% success rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #161: File Manager freezes during copy, move and delete, with no progress indication
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.45.16.mov

What happens

Copying a large file to a network share — or deleting on one — freezes the entire window for the whole operation. No repaint, no input, no indication that anything is happening. On a Tailscale-backed SMB mount measured at ~1.1 MB/s, a 72 MB panorama is roughly 65 seconds of a dead window, which is indistinguishable from a hang.

Root cause: copy_sources, move_sources and delete_sources in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs are declared #[tauri::command] without async. Tauri runs a non-async command on the main thread, so the transfer blocks the event loop. This is a real freeze, not just a missing spinner. remove_images in the same file already uses the correct async fn + injected AppHandle signature.

Separately, none of the three report progress. The shared ProgressModal (src/renderer/components/modals/ProgressModal.tsx) already exists but is only driven by rotate, duplicate and image-centering.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a slow network share (SMB over a VPN/tunnel makes it obvious).
  2. Open File Manager and point one panel at the share.
  3. Copy a file of 50 MB or more into it.
  4. The window stops responding until the copy finishes. Nothing on screen indicates progress or that the app is still alive.

Deleting several files on the same share shows the same freeze.

Goal

  1. The window stays responsive during copy, move and delete.
  2. A progress modal appears for operations slow enough to be noticeable, and always closes when the operation ends — including on failure. An operation that opens a modal and never closes it is worse than no modal.
  3. Copy and move progress is measured in bytes, not files. A File Manager selection is usually a handful of very large panoramas — often exactly one — so a file counter would sit at 0% for the entire transfer and then jump to 100%.
  4. Delete reports file counts instead: trashing is a rename, so its cost scales with entry count, not size.
  5. Fast local operations do not flash a modal on screen.
  6. The existing rotate / duplicate / image-centering progress behaviour is unchanged.

QA Summary — Passed

QA date: 2026-09-02
Target: GoThru Photo Studio desktop app (Tauri v2 + Rust) / Issue #161 — File Manager progress & non-blocking window during copy, move, delete
Verdict: Passed.

Executive Summary

Comprehensive real-device testing on Windows 11 with live mapped SMB shares (Z:\), UNC volumes, and local folders confirms full resolution of Issue #161:

  1. Async Execution & Responsive Window: copy_sources, move_sources, and delete_sources in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs are now fully asynchronous (#[tauri::command] pub async fn), preventing the main UI thread from freezing during long-running network transfers.
  2. Progress Reporting by Bytes and Files: Copy and move operations report progress tracked in bytes (handling large single panoramas smoothly), while delete operations report file counts.
  3. Modal Lifecycle & Threshold: queueProgress.ts enforces FILE_OPERATION_MODAL_DELAY = 250ms so fast local operations execute silently without flickering a modal, while long transfers display ProgressModal and reliably close upon completion or failure.

All test scenarios (TC-01 through TC-03) executed and passed on the real application with 100% success rate.
